data.narrative:
ElectroFlow Technologies is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Eric McShane and Evan Gardner that has raised $10M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (LNZA) in the climate and energy sector, including notable private companies such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression approach is applicable to this valuation. Using the $10M total raised as a proxy for current implied value and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied value of $25M. This method is appropriate given the limited peer set at the exact seed stage and similar valuation tier within the climate and energy sector. A peer-median approach was not viable: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints when filtered by stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier proximity. Applying an all-sector median would introduce undue noise.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $21M (low) to $29M (high), with a median of $25M. This single-method range reflects the absence of robust peer comparables at ElectroFlow's stage and tier. Key uncertainties center on the scarcity of narrow-set comps and the reliance on a simplified progression assumption rather than market-derived benchmarks. Validation would benefit from additional seed-stage or Series A transactions in the climate tech space.
